analysis.time_in_compute_note: the sum of vulkan.subgraph spans — the EP's own view of time inside Compute. record_scaling.composition_note: vulkan.record is not one activity. It brackets vkBeginCommandBuffer through vkEndCommandBuffer, and the host memcpy of this island's inputs into staging buffers happens inside it. The two are reported separately because they have different fixes: the memcpy goes away if the data stops being re-copied per Compute call; the residual is the recording loop itself.
record_scaling.size_detail: steady-state medians by dispatch count: record {'1': 13.053, '10': 50.637} ms, of which command construction {'1': 0.2775, '10': 0.4635} ms; mean upload bytes per island size {'1': 15931392.0, '10': 64959360.0}. Dispatch count spans 10×, record median spans 3.9×. Spearman(dispatches, record) = 0.2613; Spearman(upload bytes, record) = 0.387. Implied record bandwidth by island size {'1': 1.1367, '10': 1.1947} GiB/s (spread 1.051×). Only 2 distinct island sizes are present in this partition, so this is a two-point comparison, not a fitted curve.
record_scaling.size_confound: the implied bandwidth is the same to within 1.051× across island sizes, while the command construction residual spans only 1.7× for a 10× change in dispatch count. Recording cost is a byte-throughput cost, not a per-dispatch cost: bigger islands record slower here because they carry more input bytes, and the apparent size effect is a bytes effect wearing a size label.
record_scaling.warmup_shape_note: cycles_to_steady is the first inference whose mean record cost is within 25% of the median of the last three. A value of 2 means the cost is a one-off paid on inference 1 and everything after it is steady state — a fixed cost to amortise, not a curve to fit.
record_scaling.decline_detail: the decline holds within island identity: 100% of islands record faster on their last inference than on their first, and the per-cycle means fall across cycles that each contain exactly the same 33 islands in the same order. It is a warmup effect, not an island-mix artifact. Shape: ONE_OFF_FIRST_INFERENCE (steady within 25% of the tail median 54.4975 ms from inference 2). It has flattened: the last three cycle means span 1.0747×, so the steady state is reached and 50.5315 ms is the median Switch is optimising against.

relabelled.why: ep.device_index indexes engine.rs::probe_devices, which is sorted best-first; vulkaninfo/probe() return enumeration order. On this laptop the two are reversed, so every row of the original table carried the other device's name and facts. Corrected from each trace's own timestampPeriod/validBits fingerprint.
relabelled.also: gpu_containment re-run with ordinal attribution; its 14 earlier violations were artefacts of a 314 ms calibration-anchor uncertainty and are gone.

withdrawn.reason: These traces were captured while other agents were compiling on the same machine. The in-band control (phases.contention_signature) compares each island slot's host record spread against that same slot's GPU busy spread across repetitions of identical work. The device clock is not affected by host CPU load; the host clock is. On ep.device_index 0 (NVIDIA RTX 4060), 20 of 33 slots recorded a >= 2x host spread while their own GPU time stayed within 1.25x -- one slot swung 190.93 -> 501.56 -> 1747.51 ms against a GPU spread of 1.0019x. Neither run was in a steady state, so every aggregate here is a mean over conditions that were not held constant. See docs/PERF.md section 10.

0.reason: 20 of 33 island slots (61%) recorded a >= 2.0x host spread across repetitions of identical work while their own GPU time stayed within 1.25x. Worst: slot 31 (10 dispatches) host 9.386x vs GPU 1.0024x. The stall is on the host, not the device: this run was not in a steady state and its aggregates are means over conditions that were not held constant

1.reason: whole inferences of identical work varied 5.251x (min 0.5102, max 2.6788 of the run median), but GPU time moved alongside on every slot, so the control cannot isolate the cause to the host. Either way the run was not in a steady state: this is not a quotable measurement, and it is not an exoneration of the machine
1.provenance: computed from bench/_scratch/phi35_trace_dev1.trace.json before that file was overwritten by a later smoke run on the same device. NOT re-derivable. Recorded verbatim rather than recomputed, because recomputing it from the current file would silently substitute a different run's numbers under this run's label.
1.integrated_gpu_caveat: This device shares its power and thermal budget with the CPU cores, so heavy CPU load can slow the GPU itself. GPU time moving with host time therefore does not exonerate the machine here; NOT_STEADY means 'not established', not 'quiet'.
